title: Did Maple Hollow cut its library budget by 40%?
claim: Maple Hollow cut its library budget by 40 percent this year.
speaker: Councilor Dana Reyes (fictional)
body: City budget documents show the library line fell from 2.0 million to 1.7 million dollars, a 15 percent reduction. The 40 percent figure counts a one-time renovation grant from the previous year as part of the regular operating budget. Library staff said opening hours were reduced by one evening per week. The council approved the budget by a 5-2 vote. Because the claim takes a real reduction and roughly triples its size by mixing one-time and recurring money, we rate it Mostly False.

title: Is the Riverton bridge closed for two years?
claim: The Riverton river bridge will be closed to all traffic for two years.
speaker: Radio host Sam Patel (fictional)
body: The state transportation agency's published schedule closes the bridge to cars for 14 weeks during deck replacement. Pedestrian and bicycle lanes stay open throughout the project. No document or official statement mentions a two-year closure. The agency said the confusion may come from an earlier proposal that was rejected in 2022. The claim is not supported by the schedule, so we rate it False.

title: Solar jobs in the fictional state of Westland doubled
claim: Solar jobs in Westland doubled over the last five years.
speaker: Governor Ada Rivera (fictional)
body: Employment data from the Westland labor department show solar installation and manufacturing jobs rose from 6,100 to 12,400 between 2019 and 2024. That is an increase of 103 percent. Independent industry surveys report a similar trend. The governor's statement is accurate and needs no additional context, so we rate it True.

title: School lunch prices and the new levy
claim: The new school levy raises lunch prices for every child.
speaker: Candidate Lee Morgan (fictional)
body: The levy funds building maintenance, not meals. However, the district approved a separate 25-cent lunch price increase in the same meeting. Children who qualify for free meals, about 38 percent of them, pay nothing. The claim links two unrelated decisions and ignores the free-meal program, but lunch prices did rise for many families. We rate it Half True.

title: Crime at a record high in Lakeside?
claim: Crime in Lakeside is at an all-time record high.
speaker: Mayor Jordan Blake (fictional)
body: Police department reports show reported crimes fell for the third straight year and are now 22 percent below the peak reached in 2008. The mayor's office did not provide a source. Repeating a claim that the official data plainly contradicts earns our lowest rating, Pants on Fire.

title: What the fluoride study actually found
claim: A new study proves tap water fluoride lowers test scores.
speaker: Blogger Riley Chen (fictional)
body: The cited study looked at fluoride concentrations far above the levels used in the region's tap water, and its authors said the results do not apply to typical community water programs. The study found an association, not proof of cause. Because it overstates both the strength and the relevance of the research, we rate the claim Mostly False.

title: Minimum wage change and teen employment
claim: Teen employment fell after Westland raised the minimum wage.
speaker: Senator Pat Okafor (fictional)
body: Teen employment did decline by 3 percent in the year after the increase. Economists we contacted noted that teen employment fell by a similar amount in neighboring states that did not change their minimum wage. The numbers are right, but the implied cause is not established. We rate it Half True.

title: Voter roll maintenance explained
claim: Lakeside removed 50,000 voters from the rolls last month.
speaker: Activist Morgan Ellis (fictional)
body: County records show 48,700 registrations were moved to inactive status after routine mail checks, not removed. Inactive voters can still vote after confirming their address. The number is close and the records were changed, but 'removed' overstates what happened. We rate it Mostly True.

title: Did bus ridership recover in Maple Hollow?
claim: Bus ridership in Maple Hollow is back above pre-pandemic levels.
speaker: Transit director Avery Kim (fictional)
body: Monthly ridership reports show 1.21 million trips in January compared with 1.15 million in January 2019. The transit agency's numbers are audited annually. The statement is accurate.

title: Is the city selling Central Meadow park?
claim: The city is selling Central Meadow park to a developer.
speaker: Neighborhood post (fictional)
body: No sale has been proposed. The council voted to lease a 0.3-acre corner of the park for a seasonal food market for one year. The park remains city property, and the lease can be ended with 30 days' notice. We rate the claim False.
